lens: release safety: confirm staged-index drift guard, durable coverage floor, pre-chain grandfathering, and child CAS resolve the prior block

findings.summary: The staged-tree drift guard detects a changed final tree, but a failed final tree inspection still permits a verdict, so staged-index identity is not established at finalization.
evidence: In run_state_drift's STAGED_HEAD branch, resolve_staged_tree(repo_root) is compared with pinned["resolved_head_sha"] only when tree_now is not None.
The accompanying comment explicitly says an unresolvable final tree skips the secondary guard.

A final git write-tree failure therefore returns no staged-tree drift when the pool fingerprint is unchanged, despite the run being unable to prove that the staged index still matches the analyzed tree.
test_staged_drift_catches_an_index_only_change covers a successfully resolved changed tree, but no test requires final resolve failure to mark the run untrusted.
findings.action: Fail closed when final resolve_staged_tree returns None and add a regression test showing final staged-tree inspection failure produces an untrusted/no-verdict result.

findings.summary: The durable coverage floor remains removable from the worker report, allowing the same thin result to validate after expected_targets is omitted.
evidence: build_report carries expected_targets and coverage_ok only as ordinary report fields; neither is joined to the receipt, ledger attempt, or provenance digest.
validate_delivered_worker_report does not require expected_targets or coverage_ok among its mandatory fields.

_validate_receipt_and_result falls back to report.get("expected_targets"); when that field is absent or null, report_declared_targets returns None and validate_bounded_result performs no coverage check.
test_durable_carrier_rejects_a_thin_file_despite_the_report preserves expected_targets in the report; it does not test removal or alteration of that declaration before durable validation.
test_durable_carrier_passes_an_undeclared_thin_result demonstrates that the resulting no-floor shape is accepted.
findings.action: Cryptographically join the normalized expected-target set or its digest into immutable attempt/receipt/report provenance, require consistency at durable validation, and add tests that deletion or alteration of the report declaration cannot make a thin result deliverable.

counterweight_triage.concern: Pre-chain Goal Runs with observed body digests could become uncloseable.
counterweight_triage.disposition: _accepted_body_digests now returns an empty set unless the item has recorded revision-chain digests, preserving historical marker-only behavior; the supplied regression covers a pre-chain edited body despite an observed digest.

counterweight_triage.concern: A concurrent child edit could be overwritten after the parent revision is recorded.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The child update now supplies expected_body_sha256 from the pre-record read, and the supplied race test verifies refusal while preserving the concurrent body.

counterweight_triage.concern: The staged drift guard now compares the pinned and final staged tree.
counterweight_triage.disposition: It catches a successfully resolved changed tree, but final inspection failure still fails open.

counterweight_triage.concern: The coverage declaration is carried into the durable report.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The durable validator reuses the declaration when present, but the declaration is optional and is not provenance-bound, so removal disables the floor.

next_move: Do not release 8.8.0 from this packet. Make final staged-tree resolution fail closed and bind the expected-target declaration into immutable delivery provenance; then add the two adversarial regressions and rerun the bounded follow-up review.
non_claims: No workspace state, test execution, or content outside the identity-bound inline payload was inspected.
This review does not dispute the supplied pre-chain grandfathering or child-CAS fixes.
This review does not assess packaging, release notes, or non-pool execution-input boundaries beyond the selected semantic input.
